name: Yolanda Diarra-Kuznetsova
location: Old Harbor, Stitch Row — a narrow commercial street off the Grindstone Shore waterfront, near Lake Shore and Navy Pier
description:
Yolanda is tall and narrow-shouldered with very dark skin, close-shaved temples, and a cloud of natural hair she wears differently every day — sometimes pinned, sometimes free, occasionally containing small objects she's tucked in absentmindedly (a seam ripper, a rolled-up measurement tape, once a small wrench she was holding for someone). Her forearms have retractable micro-filament guides — a geneware mod she had installed specifically for this work, allowing her to feel tension in fabric the way a surgeon feels tissue. Her irises are a vivid violet that is very obviously engineered and that she picked because, as she says, if you're going to do it you might as well commit.

She runs a small shop — Stitch Row No. 4 — that does everything from emergency repairs to full commission builds, with a specialty in structural garments: clothes with hidden pockets, sealed linings, insulated layers, things that need to function as well as look good. She is quick and funny and gives blunt assessments of what will and won't work on a person's body with the cheerful directness of someone who has long since stopped worrying about whether people find her charming. She has a loyal client base that includes everyone from dock workers needing reinforced work gear to people who have heard about her discreet interior construction and want to know what she can do with a coat lining.

core_fears: Losing the dexterity to do this work — the geneware failing, her hands going
The shop failing and having to work for someone else
core_desires: To build something that outlasts her — an apprenticeship program, a school, something
To be known for craft, not just utility
coping_mechanisms: Working — she does her best thinking with her hands occupied
Gallows humor; she jokes about bad things before they can ambush her
blind_spots: She sometimes trusts people's aesthetics more than their character — if they have good taste she assumes they're good
psychology.secret: She has been making, at no charge, a garment for the past eight months — a full ceremonial outfit in traditional styles blending Malian and Russian textile traditions, sized for her estranged mother. She doesn't know if she'll ever send it. She keeps it in a sealed box under the counter.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical fabric and construction terms that she deploys casually, assuming people know them. Socially fluent and funny in a dry way. Occasional untranslated phrases from the Bambara and Russian she grew up hearing.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, layered — two or three things happening in a sentence. Drops words that don't need to be there.
verbal_tics: Humming while working — stops abruptly when she wants to make a point
'That's fighting the fabric.' (used for anything she considers misguided)
Stating prices as facts, not offers — non-negotiable tone
example_lines: 'You want the pocket on the left. You always reach left. I watched you. Left pocket.'
'I can do what you're describing but it's going to fight the fabric every day you wear it and eventually the fabric wins. Up to you.'

story_hooks: A client came in for alterations to a coat and left without it — abandoned it mid-appointment and hasn't returned. The coat has a concealed lining she didn't construct. She's curious about what's in it and whether she should be.

Someone is trying to set up a competing shop on Stitch Row with prices that are impossible unless they're subsidized — and they're specifically undercutting her specialty services. She wants to know why.
The ceremonial garment under the counter — she's received word that her mother is ill. Now she has to decide whether to send it, deliver it herself, or do nothing.
narrative_function: Practical services provider (can create or modify gear, conceal objects in garments). Social hub — hears things clients say when they're being measured and their guard is down. Can be a quest giver around things she's learned through the shop.
augmentations: Retractable micro-filament sensory guides (geneware, occupational-cosmetic hybrid — fingertips and inner forearms). Engineered violet irises (cosmetic geneware). No chrome.
daily_life: Shop opens at 09:00 and she's usually there by 08:00 cutting. Closes when the work is done, which varies. Thursdays she closes at noon and takes the rest of the day for herself — sacred, non-negotiable.

decision_rules: The work has to be right — she will redo something rather than release it flawed
Never ask what something is for; price for the work, not the purpose
escalation_ladder: Stop engaging and let the silence work
Remove the person from the shop — physically if necessary, she's not small

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally direct — assesses what they need fast and starts solving it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Easier and warmer; teases them, remembers everything about their body and what works on them

stress_responses.medium: Closes the shop early and does hand-work alone for hours
stress_responses.high: Sits with the sealed box under the counter for a long time without opening it

contradictions: Claims the shop is just a business but has a deeply personal relationship with every piece she makes
Says she doesn't do charity work but has a category of clients she charges almost nothing
habits: Leaves a spool of thread at the E.L.F. shrine outside her shop every Monday — an old habit from her mother she's never stopped
Takes precise measurements even for simple repairs — she keeps records going back years
breaking_points: Someone trying to use her work to harm someone she knows
Being asked to falsify or destroy her records for someone else's convenience

timeline.event: Born in Old Harbor to a Malian-descended mother and Russian-descended father
Estrangement from mother following an undisclosed conflict
Opens Stitch Row No. 4 with savings and a small community loan
Gets micro-filament geneware installed — transforms quality and speed of her work
Begins work on the ceremonial garment for her mother

physical_description.build: Tall and narrow-shouldered with long, lean limbs; posture suggests years of leaning over work tables. Wiry muscle definition in forearms from precise, repetitive hand work.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with occasional gray threads
physical_description.hair_style: Worn variably — sometimes pinned up, sometimes loose and cloud-like; temples closely shaved on rotating sides; frequently contains small objects tucked absentmindedly (seam rippers, measurement tape coils, tools)
physical_description.hair_length: Medium to Long, with regularly maintained short sides
physical_description.eye_color: Vivid engineered violet — striking, obviously geneware, unwavering in intensity
physical_description.skin_tone: Very dark, deep brown complexion with warm undertones
physical_description.complexion: Clear, work-marked skin with calluses on fingertips and the heel of her dominant hand; minimal grooming pretension; face carries the relaxed directness of someone past the age of performing charm
distinguishing_marks: Fine white scar lines along both inner forearms where micro-filament guides were installed, visible when sleeves are rolled
Needle-prick scars scattered across fingertips and palms — the accumulated record of decades of hand-sewing
A small burn mark on her left wrist (pale, old) in the shape of a seam ripper handle
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retractable micro-filament sensory guides running along inner forearms and fingertips — visible as faint metallic threading beneath skin when active, resembling delicate subcutaneous circuitry. Engineered violet irises with no pupil dilation lag, clearly artificial but not crude. No visible chrome or external hardware.
physical_description.posture_movement: Naturally leans forward slightly, shoulders curled inward from work-table hours. Hands move with surgical precision even when idle; fingers occasionally twitch or flex unconsciously. When standing still, weight shifts to balls of feet — ready-stance of someone who works standing. Walks with economical, purposeful strides.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 utilitarian with a craftsperson's signature: well-maintained work apron worn over modified clothes; layered basics in neutral tones (charcoal, cream, deep navy); visible stitching and seaming details that are clearly intentional personal modifications. Frequently wears her own designs — fitted vests with hidden pockets, reinforced shoulder pieces, sealed linings. Sensible footwear, broken in. No jewelry except occasionally a thimble on her thumb. Sleeves often rolled to forearms, exposing the faint augmentation scarring.
